panels.description: This charts how long each completed backup run took, from its recorded run. A steady duration is normal; a sharp increase can mean the nightly backup is slowing. Read docs/runbooks/backup-restore.md §3.

targets.rawSql: SELECT at AS time, (detail->>'duration_s')::double precision / 60.0 AS duration_min FROM audit_log WHERE kind = 'backup_run' AND detail->>'phase' = 'applied' ORDER BY at

panels.title: Backup run duration

panels.description: This charts the size of files in each completed backup set, excluding the database backup repository, from the set inventory. A stable size is expected; sudden growth can consume the space kept for backups. Read docs/runbooks/backup-restore.md §3.

targets.rawSql: SELECT at AS time, (detail->>'set_bytes')::double precision AS set_bytes FROM audit_log WHERE kind = 'backup_run' AND detail->>'phase' = 'applied' ORDER BY at

panels.title: Backup set bytes

panels.description: This shows the share of sampled files reused from the previous local backup set rather than copied again, from the backup's link check. Some reuse is expected after the first set; zero reused files with a previous sample makes the run fail. Read docs/runbooks/backup-restore.md §3.

targets.rawSql: SELECT at AS time, CASE WHEN jsonb_typeof(detail->'hard_links') = 'object' THEN (detail->'hard_links'->>'linked')::double precision / NULLIF((detail->'hard_links'->>'sampled')::double precision, 0) ELSE (detail->>'hard_links')::double precision END AS hard_link_ratio FROM audit_log WHERE kind = 'backup_run' AND detail->>'phase' = 'applied' ORDER BY at

panels.title: Hard-link ratio

panels.description: This charts the share of the set's bytes each recorded push sent off the box. A first push may send everything. The line marks the 90 percent the push rule measures after setting aside bytes new to the set since the previous snapshot, so a push after a large intake can stand above the line and still have passed. A push over an unchanged set near the line means snapshots stopped sharing one target tree. The byte figures are in the runs table. Read docs/runbooks/backup-restore.md §3.

targets.rawSql: SELECT at AS time, (detail->>'transferred_bytes')::double precision / NULLIF((detail->>'total_bytes')::double precision, 0) AS transferred_share FROM audit_log WHERE kind = 'backup_push' ORDER BY at

panels.title: Push transferred share of total bytes

panels.description: This charts paths checked on the backup target from each recorded push and old target snapshots removed from the prune's own row. Checked paths show the copy was verified, while zero removed snapshots is normal when none has expired; a failed check prevents a successful push row. A night ending at the prune's deadline is normal; removal resumes the next night. Pruned reads on the right-hand axis at its own scale. The quarterly full re-hash (backup push --verify-all) checks every path, so its verified count stands far above the nightly sample's. Read docs/runbooks/backup-restore.md §3.

targets.rawSql: SELECT at AS time, verified, pruned FROM (SELECT at, (detail->>'verified')::double precision AS verified, NULL::double precision AS pruned FROM audit_log WHERE kind = 'backup_push' UNION ALL SELECT at, NULL::double precision AS verified, (detail->>'removed')::double precision AS pruned FROM audit_log WHERE kind = 'backup_prune') AS counts ORDER BY at

panels.title: Verified and pruned counts

panels.description: This charts how long each backup restore drill took, from its recorded run. A steady duration is expected; a sharp increase can make the next scheduled drill harder to finish. Read docs/runbooks/backup-restore.md §3.

targets.rawSql: SELECT at AS time, (detail->>'duration_s')::double precision / 60.0 AS duration_min FROM audit_log WHERE kind = 'backup_drill' ORDER BY at

panels.title: Restore drill duration

panels.description: This table lists the five newest recorded backup drill results. Pass means the restore checks succeeded; failed means they did not and causes a page. Follow docs/runbooks/observability.md §4.

targets.rawSql: SELECT at, detail->>'result' AS result FROM audit_log WHERE kind = 'backup_drill' ORDER BY at DESC LIMIT 5

panels.title: Restore drill result

panels.description: This charts how long each recorded push took, from its row. The first push after a new set form or a target restore copies more and takes longer; a steady duration is expected after it. Read docs/runbooks/backup-restore.md §3.

targets.rawSql: SELECT at AS time, (detail->>'duration_s')::double precision / 3600.0 AS duration_h FROM audit_log WHERE kind = 'backup_push' ORDER BY at

panels.title: Push duration

panels.description: This table lists the ten newest recorded backup runs, pushes, drills, and restores with each result, sizes, and the share of sampled files reused. A run, push, or restore reads completed when healthy; a healthy drill reads pass. A failed drill or a missing expected run needs investigation. Read docs/runbooks/backup-restore.md §3.

targets.rawSql: SELECT at, kind, (detail->>'duration_s')::double precision AS duration_s, COALESCE(detail->>'result', 'completed') AS result, (detail->>'set_bytes')::bigint AS set_bytes, CASE WHEN jsonb_typeof(detail->'hard_links') = 'object' THEN (detail->'hard_links'->>'linked')::double precision / NULLIF((detail->'hard_links'->>'sampled')::double precision, 0) ELSE (detail->>'hard_links')::double precision END AS hard_link_ratio, (detail->>'transferred_bytes')::bigint AS transferred_bytes, (detail->>'total_bytes')::bigint AS total_bytes, (detail->>'verified')::integer AS verified, COALESCE(detail->>'removed', detail->>'pruned')::integer AS pruned FROM audit_log WHERE kind IN ('backup_run', 'backup_push', 'backup_prune', 'backup_drill', 'restore') AND (kind <> 'backup_run' OR detail->>'phase' = 'applied') ORDER BY at DESC LIMIT 10

panels.title: Last ten backup and restore runs
